prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop portfolio decision comp, first viewport only, 16:10 landscape
Primary request: Design a polished recruiter-facing personal portfolio homepage for Võ Hoàng Anh Quân, handle K1llV, an Information Security student. Art direction is “Security Audit Dossier”: a contemporary editorial security assessment document that feels credible, intentional, and highly scannable, while remaining unmistakably a modern website.
Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed flat off-white report stock background #f7f6f2, with subtle paper grain only. No device frame and no environmental scene.
Subject: The portfolio UI itself. Build a disciplined asymmetrical editorial grid with generous margins and clear section boundaries. Top navigation should retain the current portfolio categories: “Profile”, “About”, “Skills”, “Projects”, “Achievements”, “Contact”. Include a compact wordmark “K1llV / PORTFOLIO” and a small status line such as “AVAILABLE FOR SECURITY & DEVELOPMENT ROLES”.
Composition/framing: Show the complete desktop first viewport at a straight-on angle, approximately 1440×900 proportions. Header is slim. Main area is split into a strong executive summary on the left and a flagship project evidence panel on the right. Use thin rules, discreet folio numbers, tiny audit tabs, restrained marginal annotations, and one small orange index marker. Keep every important element comfortably inside the frame.
Executive summary exact text: “VÕ HOÀNG ANH QUÂN”; “INFORMATION SECURITY STUDENT”; “I build secure, dependable digital products by connecting security thinking with practical full-stack engineering.” Add two clear actions: “VIEW CV” and “EMAIL ME”.
Flagship evidence exact text: “FLAGSHIP FINDING 01”; “YOCA”; “Full-stack Developer”; “A Solana product built with React and TypeScript.” Add evidence tags “SOLANA”, “REACT”, “TYPESCRIPT” and a compact link label “REVIEW PROJECT”.
Supporting microcopy may include only short, readable labels such as “PROFILE / 2026”, “FOCUS / APPLICATION SECURITY”, “LOCATION / VIETNAM”, and “SELECTED EVIDENCE”. Do not invent employers, metrics, certifications, awards, contact details, or security findings.
Style/medium: High-fidelity UI mockup, refined editorial art direction, exacting Swiss-influenced grid, modern cybersecurity report language without costume or cliché. Typography must be a distinctive contemporary sans-serif, not Inter; use an assertive grotesk for display and a clean technical sans for supporting copy. No serif type. Name should be visually dominant. Use uppercase selectively, not everywhere.
Lighting/mood: Flat digital interface with tactile print-document restraint; sober, confident, precise, recruiter-friendly.
Color palette: off-white #f7f6f2, near-black #171717, singular signal orange #d24a2f. Orange appears only on the primary action, one index marker, and a few tiny functional accents. No other colors.
Materials/textures: restrained report-paper texture, hairline rules, crisp typography, no glossy effects.
Constraints: Maintain strong readable copy and real UI spacing. CV and Email actions must be unmistakable. The YOCA panel must clearly and truthfully show Full-stack Developer, Solana, React, and TypeScript. Preserve an understated audit dossier motif with tabs and annotations, but no heavy decoration.
Avoid: detective imagery, magnifying glasses, fingerprints, caution tape, police folders, hacker masks, matrix code, terminal windows, command-line interfaces, neon, gradients, glassmorphism, fake screenshots, fake code, excessive stamps, distressed grunge, crowded dashboards, serif fonts, Inter font, illegible microtext, em dash characters, watermark, logos from real companies.
